label: Trigger
gloss: something arrives, or a clock fires, and a run starts
why: Nothing in an automation happens until something starts it. A trigger names the event the flow waits for, and every record it emits becomes one run. At Beacon, the invoice desk flow starts when an invoice lands in the Invoice Inbox - no trigger, no run, and INV-1 just sits there.
cue: whenever work begins on its own - an email lands, a file drops, a timer hits - look for the trigger; if there is not one, the automation has not started yet
task: Make the flow start when an invoice lands in the Invoice Inbox, so INV-1 enters a run.
notes: A flow always begins with a Trigger - it is the only step allowed first.
Event mode: one run per record that arrives in the source.
Schedule mode: one run at a set time, with no record from a source.

checks.label: INV-1 entered a run
checks.why: a trigger on the Invoice Inbox emits one record per invoice
